Move journal

Moves & help
Your moves will appear here. Try a ring or press Randomize.

Every ring turn is a legal cube move.

How to play & keyboard shortcuts

The highlighted ring and cube slice are linked. Choose an outer face or an inner slice.

Make all six cube faces a single color. Choose a letter button, then press either turn arrow. You can also select an exposed ring curve and drag along it; release after a short arc for one quarter-turn. “Focus selected rings” enlarges the selected ring.

There are 6 independently movable layers on each axis. L R U D F B are the outer layers. Ri is the second layer in from the right; Rii, when present, is the third. Each control turns just one layer. There is no single middle slice on this even cube.

The 216 dots are all 216 stickers. Every dot sits at a crossing of two rings. Each ring carries a belt of 24 stickers. An outer turn also rotates the 36 stickers on its face; an inner turn moves only its belt. The 3D view highlights the selected slice. Select “Focus selected rings” to inspect one belt more closely.

Use ← and → to turn the selected ring. Keys U D L R F B turn outer layers; hold Alt for the adjacent inner slice, and Shift to reverse. Select deeper slices using their ring buttons. On odd cubes, M E S turn the middle slices. A prime (′) means inverse and 2 means a half-turn. Letters use clockwise notation viewed from that side; arrow buttons follow the ring’s on-screen direction.

Drag the cube to look around and scroll or pinch to zoom. With the cube focused, arrow keys rotate the view and +/− zoom. Camera movement never turns a slice.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies 72 legal outer and inner slice turns with a fresh seed every time. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. The seed records the generated sequence. The journal uses a prime (′) for inverse moves and 2 for half-turns, so Rii2 means a half-turn of the third layer in from the right.
